neighbours.label: The word that completes a fixed 'X of ___' name, above all a big city right after 'University of' (University of⟦ Sydney⟧, ⟦ Paris⟧, ⟦ London⟧, ⟦ Tokyo⟧, ⟦ Vienna⟧) and ' prey' in 'bird of prey'. The same city or 'prey' outside the frame stays quiet.
fire: My aunt taught chemistry at the University of Sydney for twenty years.
The manuscript is kept in the library of the University of Paris.
He turned down an offer from the University of London to stay at home.
Two researchers from the University of Tokyo presented the results.
The falcon is the fastest bird of prey in the world.
After the war she enrolled at the University of Vienna to study medicine.
Eagles, hawks and other birds of prey nest along these cliffs.
The survey was run by a team at the University of Sydney last year.
quiet: My aunt taught chemistry at a high school in Sydney for twenty years.
The manuscript is kept in a small library in Paris.
He turned down an offer from a bank in London to stay at home.
Two researchers who live in Tokyo presented the results.
The falcon dives on its prey at tremendous speed.
After the war she moved to Vienna to study medicine.
Eagles, hawks and other large birds nest along these cliffs.
The survey was run by a team at the university last year.

notes: Card: ' Sydney' x5, ' Paris' x3, ' London' x3, ' Tokyo' x2 after 'University of', ' prey' x2 after 'bird(s) of'. Probes: 'bird of prey' 0.94, 'University of Sydney' 0.49, Vienna 0.40, Tokyo 0.37, Melbourne 0.30; weaker for other 'X of place' names (Bank of London 0.25, University of Texas 0.20, Royal Society of Edinburgh 0.17, University of Michigan 0.15); 'city of Paris' 0.06, 'London to Sydney' 0.01, 'its prey' 0.02. So the frame matters more than the city; what the cities and 'prey' share is closing a well-known 'noun of ___' collocation. The + pole (' which' after 'of', ' dont') looks unrelated.
